# Tasks — Android

Download [Tasks 0.90.0](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Tasks-v0.90.0.apk). Install over the existing app to retain your tasks and settings.

Task editors now use rounded square label tiles with icons and names. Selected labels and priority buttons have white outlined glows; the visible priority radio circles are removed. Widget Quick add has the same larger label choices.

Successful swipes between Today and Upcoming give the same short haptic pulse as Relationship Manager. Short or cancelled swipes stay silent.

Settings → Task ordering now offers Hold and drag alongside the existing arrows. Hold a task for 380ms to lift its full card, then drag vertically while the other cards move aside around its drop space, matching Relationship Manager. Priority changes, urgent ordering, saved positions, cancelled drags and failed-save recovery are preserved. The Weekend shortcut always chooses the next Friday strictly after today, including when used on Friday, Saturday or Sunday.

In-progress tasks move as full cards to the top of Today, replacing the separate title-only banner. Their details, checklist, completion checkbox and actions stay available. Stopping a task returns it to its normal priority section and saved position. Multiple active tasks appear there together; linked and checklist progress retain their existing behavior.

Web links in displayed task notes open in your browser. Detailed Edit task and Add task forms place Time on the left and Date on the right. Contexts stays under Priority/Urgent; Notify stays under Time; Hide until before due time and its lead-time fields span the full width below both Time and Date. The Repeat starts note is removed. The helper sentence is removed and vertical spacing is slightly tighter. Task arrow moves use a noticeable 350 ms fade. The widget keeps its plain Overdue label while its green active pill shows only IN PROGRESS.

Task arrows use a single tap to move one task, a double tap to change priority one level, and a hold to jump to High or Low. A single up-click at a section edge enters the bottom of the higher priority; a single down-click enters the top of the lower priority. Double taps and holds enter a different priority at its bottom. Holding Up while already High moves to its top; holding Down while already Low moves to its bottom. Successful actions give haptic feedback. Unmoved tasks default to creation time, oldest first. Saved order applies to Today, Upcoming and the widget; Urgent tasks remain first.

Unfinished tasks carry into following days in their normal priority lists with an Overdue from date line beneath their details. This includes missed recurring occurrences. Completing an overdue task completes only that occurrence and keeps later repeats intact. The widget also includes unfinished past tasks. Tasks scheduled for the future stay on their selected dates.

Task editors show a subtle creation date in the top-right corner. Creation timestamps are saved for new app and widget tasks, preserved through edits and rescheduling, and recovered from older app IDs when possible. Tasks with no creation history say Created date unavailable. Revealed hidden-task borders now clear their checkbox, and Hide until before due time sits below Date and Time, above Duration.

Upcoming and reminders follow the selected dates and weekdays. Today and the widget include scheduled occurrences, explicit moves and unfinished past occurrences. Friday previews remain removed. Upcoming shows later repeats even if an older occurrence is unfinished. Recurring schedules ignore obsolete day-move entries. A refresh icon beside Settings reloads saved tasks and refreshes native widgets/reminders; the calendar also updates at midnight and on focus.

The persistent in-progress notification now has a Complete action. It completes a single active task directly, or lets you choose a task when several are active. The task list, history and widget share the completion.

Upcoming uses actual occurrence dates: Sunday-only repeats stay on Sunday, and Saturday–Sunday repeats appear under those days rather than Friday. Future editors retain the selected date and weekdays. The app remembers your last Today/Upcoming tab. Upcoming includes tasks with a future reveal time; Today’s Hidden button temporarily reveals them with a white outline. The app’s empty-list messages are left-aligned. The widget centers the visible text and flower together using its current width, with a wider, shorter default size for new widgets. The launcher controls the outer grid placement; existing widgets can be resized with its handles.

Download the [Windows installer 0.90.0](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Tasks-Setup-v0.90.0.exe). Windows now supports adding and editing tasks, Today/Upcoming, projects, priorities, labels, repeat schedules, notes, checklists, completion/progress, rescheduling, ordering and theme settings. A new PC works offline immediately with an empty list and history; pairing preserves tasks already created on the PC. The main Add task plus button is now borderless, with its size and fill unchanged.

For cloud sync, update and open your current phone first. An already connected phone uses its current task list as the initial corrected cloud list. If prompted, choose Use this phone’s tasks. Wait for Settings → Google sync to say Synced with Google. Other clients restore that cloud list on first sign-in instead of merging in an old local list; a private local backup is made before replacement. Later edits and deletions synchronize both ways.

Windows also needs its Google Desktop client configuration. In [Google Cloud → Clients](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients), select Tasks and download the JSON for the Desktop app client. In Windows Tasks, use Settings → Google sync → Set up Google to import that file locally, then sign into the same account as the phone. Configuration and refresh tokens are protected with Windows user encryption. The connected account row shows email, status, Sync now and an × to remove the account. [Setup and restore details](docs/GOOGLE-SIGN-IN-SETUP.md).

The home-screen Refresh button requests Google sync on Android and Windows, just like Sync now in Settings. It also refreshes local tasks. Windows saves pending window edits before requesting cloud sync; the home page reports the sync result or a connection/setup issue. Without a Google account, local refresh still works.

Local QR pairing remains available under Settings → Local pairing. Keep both apps open on the same Wi-Fi for LAN sync. Google sync runs while the Android app is in the foreground and while the PC background process is running; local edits remain saved during outages. [Portable Windows executable](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Tasks-PC-v0.90.0.exe) · [Windows instructions](desktop/USING-TASKS-PC.txt).

The per-user installer, application identity and taskbar pinning remain stable. Updates and uninstall preserve personal task data and account/pairing files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Tasks`. [Installer verification](docs/WINDOWS-INSTALLER-VALIDATION.md) · [Taskbar verification](docs/WINDOWS-TASKBAR-VALIDATION.md).

A personal Android checklist based on the supplied task list. The app includes the original task definitions and saved history, works offline, and keeps existing installed data when updated.

- Notes and Checklist use direct corner resizing with touch, mouse and keyboard support; the separate size slider is removed. The Settings gradient stays anchored to the visible viewport as the dialog scrolls.
- Editor groups such as Repeat, Contexts, Linked tasks and Priority use no outer box and align with the left edge of the other fields. Individual input and choice-button outlines remain visible.
- Icons align vertically with their captions and label spacing uses consistent 6 px gaps. Native label-picker images center with text, and Guild uses a compact fixed 20 dp crest. The widget editor dims the status-bar gap while retaining safe top clearance. Notes and Checklist resize directly from their corner grips; [Raid] and [Discord] lines create dividers, while [] returns to ungrouped items. Section edits preserve item completion identities and future recurrences.
- Refined white icons share one 24 px canvas and rounded corners/tips. The clock has equal-length hands clear of the rim, repeat arrows have distinct rounded heads, the chain uses rounded interlocking links, and Outdoors uses a rounded tree canopy. Custom emoji sizing is preserved.
- Simple clock, recurrence and chain-link symbols are larger and use white strokes on a transparent background. The original Home, Road, Phone, Computer and Outdoors labels also use solid white pictograms, with custom emoji overrides and the Guild crest preserved. Settings → Notifications offers separate title and message fields for the daily reminder, alongside its existing time and enable switch; timed task templates stay independent.
- The full date stays on one line beside Today and Upcoming. Tabs use a compact 44 px height, slightly less horizontal padding and a small amount of extra header width. Header text retains its original size when space allows and fits proportionally only when needed. Task details keep their font size and wrap by component, with separator dots clipped at line boundaries. Priority text reads Low, Med and High.
- New tasks default to Low in the app and widget. Existing unset tasks appear in Low with their details and history intact. Only High, Medium and Low sections remain; the removed priority count no longer appears in the header. Widget editors reserve space below the Android notification bar.
- Task history now has separate Show completed and Show trash controls. Deleted tasks can be restored with notes and history intact. Each completed or trashed entry has a two-tap Delete forever icon with a three-second confirmation timeout; deleting a completed recurring entry leaves future recurrences intact. Permanent-removal records prevent stale widget snapshots from restoring deleted entries.
- Upcoming groups start collapsed. Task notes saved in the detailed editor appear beneath the task metadata. The obsolete Grooming instruction is removed; custom notes are retained. Task details read duration · time · recurrence · labels · low/med/high. The summary separates untimed tasks with a dot.
- Settings → Task detail icons chooses Emojis (default), Simple symbols or Off for duration, recurrence and linked-task icons. Labels retain their chosen emoji or image. Settings → Notifications customizes the global timed-task notification title and message; {task}, {time} and {date} insert task details. The daily reminder stays separate.
- Priority changes and task deletion briefly fade before rows move. Dialogs lock background scrolling and retain a thin border. The widget editor has less top spacing, while native widget quick-add fields allow more vertical room for text.
- Settings → Changelog shows the full published update history, newest first. Historical releases can be expanded individually. Widget task actions and the header provide light haptics, respecting the phone’s touch-feedback setting. Text buttons, dropdowns and editable fields are left-aligned; control contents are vertically centered and icon controls retain their centered layout.
- Hold the date to open Projects without adding a third tab. Projects are notes with an optional date and duration, no labels, time or checkboxes. Tap a project to edit, complete, reopen or delete it; the outline trash icon turns red on the first tap, resets to gray after three seconds, and deletes on a second tap within that window. Projects have their own plus and completed list. Make task copies the idea into one Low priority task and archives the project, retaining its notes. Project data stays separate from task progress and widgets.
- Tap a widget task title to open the exact app editor as a rounded home-screen overlay. Save updates the shared task definition and widget immediately; daily edits carry forward. Cancel, Back, and tapping outside close it without saving, and the keyboard stays closed until a text field is tapped. Widget checkboxes and Today / In progress badges keep their separate actions.
- Opens on Today, with a date-only header and corner plus for Quick add. Only Quick add opens the keyboard automatically. Detailed task creation and editing focus the dialog and collapse the keyboard until a text field is tapped. Their action buttons stay visible in a reserved footer while the fields scroll above it. Existing tasks have an outline trash button: the first tap turns it red without adding text, confirmation expires after three seconds, and a second tap deletes the definition from current and future lists. Input changes reset confirmation; stored completion history remains intact. Tap outside either task editor to dismiss it without saving.
- Task checkboxes use the chosen accent color, centered vertically against task titles, including wrapped titles and checklist steps. Mobile text autosizing is disabled. Drag horizontally between Today and Upcoming: both panels follow the finger and settle on release, with short drags returning to the starting tab. reduced-motion settings skip the animation. Tab taps switch immediately; vertical scrolling and taps on interactive controls retain their usual behavior. Horizontal drags can start on task controls, including time, repeat, labels, checkboxes and the gear, without activating their tap actions. Both screens share task-row markup, fonts and spacing; duration and other details sit below the title. Duration and repeat frequency stay side by side, with time wrapping separately when needed. Subtask Do now buttons share the visible outline of parent task controls. Only the checkbox changes completion; titles, checklist titles and labels do not. Tap a label emoji to edit the task’s labels, or tap the displayed time, repeat frequency or duration for a focused popup that preserves the rest of the task. Inline shortcuts suppress blue touch highlights and text selection; keyboard focus stays visible with a neutral outline. Completion saves immediately, pauses for two seconds for undo, then hides the task without an extra undo note. Urgent badges are red and sit beside the task title when space permits, using the same spacing and vertical centering as In progress. Each badge moves below the title only when it cannot fit, without squeezing the title. The top summary shows the completion fraction and remaining duration in hours and minutes, with no redundant pending count; untimed tasks are shown separately. New tasks default to Low priority. Detailed editors offer only High, Medium and Low. Show completed opens the completed list with today’s completions highlighted first; the button has no count.
- Guild has a static image label extracted from frame zero of the supplied v8 GIF, with transparent corners. The crest is slightly larger than the standard emoji glyphs, about 24% larger than its original display size, in task rows, choices, the selected filter, native pickers and the widget summary. The existing Guild task gains the label while retaining its other edits and contexts. The image is also available in the label icon picker.
- Contexts use emojis: 🏠 🚗 📱 💻 🌳. Choose existing contexts on tasks; add custom contexts and choose their emoji in Settings. Use a palette or an emoji from your keyboard. Changing a label emoji updates existing tasks, the filter and native widget/quick-add pickers while retaining the label identity.
- Use the native time picker and Tomorrow / Weekend shortcuts alongside the date picker. Weekend selects Friday, including the current weekend’s Friday on Saturday or Sunday. Edit duration with larger, full-width Hours and Minutes boxes. Notes and Checklist stay expanded on separate rows. Lists show durations without numbering or the word total.
- Labels and normal edits are saved to a task definition and carry forward to its future daily recurrences. Checklist changes apply from the edited occurrence onward; completion is stored per occurrence.
- Repeat with Every X days, weeks, months, or years, or choose Daily, Weekdays, or Weekends. Clean out truck shows Sunday–Thursday.
- Upcoming includes each future daily occurrence even when the task is pending on Today; other work currently pending on Today stays excluded. Tomorrow has a Tomorrow plus ordinal date heading; later dates show their full weekday name plus ordinal date, in separate frameless dropdowns without divider lines. Upcoming tasks have checkboxes, visible Do now state and a Do today button with a left-facing arrow. Do today moves only the selected occurrence, preserves its completion identity and repeating definition, removes it from Upcoming and updates Today and the widget.
- Add, rename, reorder or remove checklist steps in Edit task. Stable step identities preserve checkmarks and completion dates; occurrences before the edit retain their original checklist.
- Android 12 and newer can enable precise reminders through Settings → Allow precise reminders. Exact alarms are used when permitted, with an inexact fallback if permission is unavailable or revoked. Returning to the app refreshes the plan. Previously armed reminders that Android has delayed survive unrelated saves for up to 24 hours; completion, Notify off, or a time/date/frequency change cancels the obsolete reminder.
- Set a task time and check Notify beside Urgent for a scheduled notification. Settings has a separate daily reminder, initially 9 AM, and independent controls for both reminder types. Android notification permission is required. Alarms resume after restart and app updates; power-saving mode or force-stop can delay/block delivery.
- Saves check commit results and reject unreadable state rather than resetting it. Local storage cannot guarantee against uninstalling, clearing data or device loss.
- Upcoming sections use month/day ordinals such as Nov 4th, including tomorrow. All date groups start collapsed.
- Tasks stay on their selected dates. Weekend repeats do not preview on Friday; every-other-week anchors and stable completion identities are preserved. The old Friday-opening setting is removed.
- Subtask summaries use a centered disclosure arrow, compact counts such as 0/4 steps, and no left border.
- Completed tasks sort by actual completion time, newest first within the existing completion-day sections. App and widget completions share durable timestamps; undo removes the timestamp and recompleting moves the task to the top. Old records without an exact timestamp fall back to their recorded completion day and saved completion-key order.
- Within each priority section, Today, Upcoming and the widget use saved manual order, or creation time (oldest first) by default. Tasks without recorded creation times retain original definition order.
- Priorities are High, Medium and Low. New tasks default to Low, and legacy unset or Lowest priorities normalize to Low; Highest becomes High. Existing task identities, details, recurring definitions and history are preserved. Each arrow stays available while a list move or priority change is possible. A single tap moves one task in the list, a double tap changes priority one level, and holding jumps to the endpoint. All successful actions give haptic feedback. Urgent tasks remain first in High before time/title sorting. Rounded square priority controls retain their existing sizing and placement.
- Buttons, inputs and menus use rounded rectangular corners; the main plus is a rounded square. App and Projects plus icons use rounded strokes painted with the app background or gradient over accent-colored buttons. The widget keeps a smaller bare accent-colored plus without a filled button or gradient, retaining a 48dp tap area and refreshing its color when the theme changes. Widget Quick Add uses the saved app colors, gradient direction, rounded panel and compact native controls with 8dp gaps between fields, side-by-side menus and buttons.
- Light haptics accompany app/Projects plus buttons, successful task creation, widget quick-add opening, and confirmed date/time selections. Feedback respects Android’s touch-feedback settings and needs no vibration permission.
- Widget Quick add supports several labels with checked selections, Today/Tomorrow/Weekend/custom dates and an optional time. After each successful add, title, labels, priority, date and time reset while the popup stays open.
- Quick add keeps its popup and keyboard ready after each saved task, clears the title, and pulses the entire white border twice without resizing the panel. This works in the app and home-screen popup. Scrollbars are hidden throughout the app and widget while touch scrolling remains available.
- The context dropdown chevron is inset 16px from the right edge.
- Horizontal swipes work across blank lower viewport space as well as task rows; dialogs and vertical scrolling retain their existing behavior.
- In-progress badges align with the title’s vertical center. In the app they sit immediately after the title with a 4px gap when there is room and stay below long titles; title checkboxes remain centered. Widget rows disable baseline alignment and extra font padding.
- Editable label emojis share the duration and repeat schedule row, wrapping only when necessary. One separator dot precedes the label section; individual labels have no separator dots. Schedule separators are slightly bolder with equal 6px spacing on each side.
- Repeating tasks have no Do today or Do tomorrow buttons in either tab; these day-move controls are available only for one-time tasks.
- Choose an unfinished task in the editor’s link dropdown to add it immediately to the selected chips. Save task persists the task and both sides of its links together. The task row shows a small 🔗 peer-title line immediately; links survive reloads and future daily recurrences. Cancel leaves saved links unchanged.
- Settings includes hex fields, swatches/color wheels, optional gradients, and a slate gradient preset. A separate viewport-sized background layer keeps the gradient visible while scrolling long lists in either tab; controls use translucent surfaces.
- The widget keeps completed rows checked for two seconds so a second checkbox tap can cancel completion. Pending requests are saved durably and recover on refresh or app resume.
- The interactive home widget is a native scrollable Today list with all open Today rows, no fixed row cap, no completed/history or upcoming rows, and a simple Today header without counts or list-name subtitles. Every row keeps its Today badge. With no open tasks, the widget centers its message against the full widget bounds with equal side margins and no extra font padding. It displays “You’re all done! Get some rest. 🪻”, matching the app. Tap a task’s Today badge to start progress; it becomes a green rounded 🟢 IN PROGRESS badge matching the app and that row moves above the widget priority sections. Tap In progress to stop and restore the row’s saved manual or creation-time position. There are no play/stop buttons. Progress stays shared with the app, but pinning affects only the widget; duplicate or stale taps do not toggle progress accidentally. Task titles use a slightly larger 13.5sp font. Quiet High/Medium/Low/Low priority sections use faint dividers. The plus is aligned to the outer right edge without a button outline, tapping the Today header opens the app, and Android’s normal long-press widget menu opens configuration. There is no gear button or footer; small internal margins let content use nearly all available space. Context/checklist filters, colors and fully transparent 0% backgrounds remain configurable; its plus opens a small home-screen form. Existing widgets switch to the new layout on update.

Multiple tasks and checklist steps can be in progress together. The top banner joins their titles with commas; stopping or completing one preserves the others. Legacy single-task progress is migrated without changing task identities.

The app is called Tasks and uses a rounded gradient checkmark icon. The Windows companion uses the same icon and task interface. Android has Internet permission for native LAN and Google sync; the packaged WebView still blocks network loads.

## Install

See [APK_BUILD.md](APK_BUILD.md) for the latest APK and [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) for verification. Requires Android 8.0 or newer. Install over the existing app; do not uninstall or clear its data.

## Build

Use JDK 21 and Android SDK Platform 35 / Build Tools 35.0.0:

```sh
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug
```

GitHub Actions also checks the real packaged UI in Chromium. Release signing keys remain outside the repository; the downloadable personal-test APK uses the retained preview signing key for in-place updates.

See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for release changes.

For each release, add the newest entry to `app/src/main/assets/changelog.json`, mirror the history in `APP_CHANGELOG` in `bridge.js` and its packaged HTML copy, and update `CHANGELOG.md`. The browser checks require the Settings history to match the packaged history and current app version.

## Route Notes

[Download Route Notes 1.0.21](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Route-Notes-v1.0.21.apk), a separate lightweight offline Android app for G200–G600 route notes. [Project and features](route-manager/README.md). Installs alongside Tasks with its own saved data and no widget.

## Meditation

[Download Meditation 1.0.16](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Meditation-v1.0.16.apk), a separate simple meditation timer with the same theme. Choose a duration and countdown, with an interval bell slider from Off to 5 bells and independent sounds/vibrations. Settings also offers color wheels, gradients, private image backgrounds and looping noise, rain or custom audio. The main screen shows just the timer, Start and a small Settings icon. Duration, sounds, vibration cues and changelog are in Settings. [Details](meditation/README.md).

## Habits

Download [Habits 1.0.7](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Habits-v1.0.7.apk). A separate, offline habit app with a resizable home-screen widget matching Tasks. Add habits in the app, then use Add widget or the launcher’s Widgets menu. Seven days span two past days, today and four upcoming days. Double tap a widget circle to cycle unmarked → X → check → unmarked; single taps leave it unchanged. Today and past days are editable; future days are read-only until their date arrives. Saved marks stay attached to their dates. Habit names remain visible with the earlier spacing. The widget shows weekday abbreviations for other days, only a dot for today, and no title or action buttons. Manage habits and widget settings in the app. [Details](habits/README.md).

## Relationship Manager

[Download RM 1.0.16](https://github.com/swettgm/task-list-android/raw/refs/heads/main/downloads/Relationship-Manager-v1.0.16.apk), a separate Android app with linked phone contacts, Friends/Family and Interests pages, tags, notes and recurring reach-out reminders. [Project details](crm/README.md) and [validation](crm/VALIDATION.md).
